diagnosis: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, NOS, germinal-center B-cell (GCB) phenotype by the Hans algorithm (CD10+, BCL6+, MUM1-). EBER negative; CD5 negative; no low-grade (follicular) component.
stage: Lugano (Ann Arbor) stage IA: a single nodal region (right cervical levels II-III, contiguous), with no B symptoms (denies fevers, night sweats and weight loss). Non-bulky: largest node 3.1 cm, well below the 7.5 cm threshold used in limited-stage trials. No extranodal, splenic or marrow disease on PET-CT. Bone marrow biopsy is not needed because PET-CT shows homogeneous marrow activity without focal uptake.
biology: Neither double-expressor nor double-hit. MYC 15% and BCL2 30% by IHC are below the 40%/50% thresholds. FISH shows no MYC, BCL2 or BCL6 rearrangement, so this is not high-grade B-cell lymphoma with MYC and BCL2 rearrangements. Ki-67 ~55%.
prognosis: IPI 0 of 5, low risk: age 45 (<=60), LDH normal (190 U/L), ECOG 0, stage I, no extranodal sites. CNS-IPI 0, low risk. Age 18-60, IPI 0 and maximum diameter <7.5 cm meet the FLYER trial eligibility criteria; expected 3-year progression-free survival is about 95%.
first_line_treatment: Curative-intent immunochemotherapy. Recommend R-CHOP every 21 days, six cycles in total, without radiotherapy, the standard full course for DLBCL. Omitting radiotherapy respects her wish to avoid neck radiation and spares the thyroid and salivary glands, a real concern given her sister's radiation-induced hypothyroidism. Acceptable alternatives: R-CHOP x3 followed by involved-site radiotherapy (ISRT), or a PET-adapted approach (S1001). Pola-R-CHP is not indicated: POLARIX enrolled IPI 2-5 only. DA-EPOCH-R is not indicated.
cns_risk: Low CNS-relapse risk: CNS-IPI 0 and no high-risk extranodal sites (kidney, adrenal, testis, breast, uterus). CNS prophylaxis is not indicated, and no MRI brain or lumbar puncture is required without neurological symptoms.
response_assessment: Interim PET-CT after cycle 3: Deauville 1-3 supports completing the plan without radiotherapy; Deauville 4-5 should prompt biopsy or consolidative ISRT rather than proceeding as planned. End-of-treatment FDG PET-CT 6-8 weeks after the last dose, read with Lugano 2014 criteria and the Deauville 5-point scale; Deauville 1-3 is a complete metabolic response. Routine surveillance imaging is not needed after a complete metabolic response.
pretreatment_workup: A pregnancy test (serum or urine hCG) is required before cycle 1; none is documented in this premenopausal woman (LMP 2026-08-28, day 21 of her cycle). Hepatitis B serology done: HBsAg and anti-HBc nonreactive (anti-HBs reactive from vaccination), so no antiviral prophylaxis is needed before rituximab. HCV and HIV nonreactive. Echo LVEF 63%, so anthracycline is permitted. Organ function and blood counts normal.
supportive_care: Stop the combined oral contraceptive (ethinyl estradiol/levonorgestrel) now: estrogen-containing contraception is contraindicated in migraine with aura because of ischemic stroke risk, and it adds venous thromboembolism risk on top of active lymphoma and chemotherapy. She still needs effective non-estrogen contraception throughout treatment and for at least 12 months after: a levonorgestrel or copper IUD is preferred (a levonorgestrel IUD also limits heavy bleeding during thrombocytopenia), or an etonogestrel implant or progestin-only pill; arrange gynecology referral and use condoms until it is in place. Fertility counselling: R-CHOP carries low gonadotoxicity at age 45 and most women resume menses, but age-related fertility decline matters; offer referral to reproductive medicine before starting since she is undecided about another pregnancy, without delaying treatment. Tumor lysis risk is low (normal LDH, uric acid and renal function); oral hydration, allopurinol optional. Primary G-CSF is not routinely required at age 45 with no risk factors, but reassess after cycle 1. Antiemetics per regimen; avoid codeine (intolerance). Rituximab infusion-reaction precautions.
fitness_and_goals: Fit: ECOG 0 with no limiting comorbidity, so curative-intent therapy is appropriate with a high cure probability. Her goals are cure, continuing to work as a teacher with minimal time off, and avoiding neck radiation; an R-CHOP plan without radiotherapy matches all three, and schedules can place infusions late in the week so she can keep teaching. Shared decision-making about the radiotherapy-containing alternative documented.

Agreed non-estrogen contraception plan for treatment and the following 12 months
Patient's fertility preference after counselling (reproductive medicine referral if wanted)

decisions.diagnosis: DLBCL NOS, GCB type (Hans); not double-expressor, not double-hit
orders_now: Serum or urine hCG pregnancy test before cycle 1
Stop combined oral contraceptive (ethinyl estradiol/levonorgestrel) now
Gynecology referral to place a levonorgestrel or copper IUD (alternatives: etonogestrel implant or progestin-only pill); condoms until it is in place
Reproductive medicine referral for fertility counselling before cycle 1, offered without delaying treatment
R-CHOP-21 x 6: rituximab 375 mg/m2 IV, cyclophosphamide 750 mg/m2 IV, doxorubicin 50 mg/m2 IV, vincristine 1.4 mg/m2 IV (max 2 mg) on day 1; prednisone 100 mg PO days 1-5; every 21 days
Oral hydration with cycle 1 (low tumor lysis risk; allopurinol optional)
conditional_orders: if interim PET-CT after cycle 3 is Deauville 4-5: biopsy or consolidative ISRT
if febrile neutropenia or a treatment delay after cycle 1: add G-CSF to subsequent cycles
if pregnancy test positive: hold chemotherapy and discuss with obstetrics before starting

lab_monitoring.tests: CBC with differential, CMP, LDH, uric acid

_expect._label: six cycles worded so the prose rule misses it ("six cycles in total"); prose still meets FLYER via the prognosis mention; decisions cycles=6 decide both items
